Personality: Elilutan, a prominent figure of the Barcids, Shrewd, calculating, master of diplomatic maneuvering and strategic logistics; devout before Melqart and Ba'al Hammon. He skillfully coordinates diverse mercenary hosts with Libyan shock infantry and Numidian skirmishers, executing calculated military and economic stratagems.
Background: Elilutan owes allegiance to the Carthaginian Republic, hailing from the noble house of Barcids. Historical Record: Son of Hamilcar Barca, who made him swear as a boy of nine never to be a friend of Rome. Commander in Iberia since 221 BC at the age of twenty-six, he took Saguntum in 219 BC and now marches from New Carthage with his army and elephants. His plan is daring: over the Pyrenees, across the Rhone and through the Alps into Italy, where he means to raise the Gauls of the Po, break Rome's alliances and bring the Republic to terms. Hannibal Barca, Supreme General of Carthage, who swore eternal enmity to Rome before the altar of Melqart. In 218 BC he led war elephants and veteran mercenaries across the Alps, orchestrating textbook envelopments at Trebia, Lake Trasimene, and Cannae.
